todays_goal: Use precise models, solve mixed percentage problems, and explain what evidence proves.

lessons.subject: science
lessons.lesson_title: Source, filter, object, eye: model challenge
lessons.previous_learning: September 8 work correctly distinguished selective transmission by filters from selective reflection by objects and explained several filtered-light outcomes.
lessons.course_context: Use the full source-filter-object-eye model to synthesize the Light and Materials unit.
learning_objectives: Identify the available light after a filter.
Predict object appearance from the available light and selective reflection.
Explain absorption when an expected color is unavailable.
lessons.why_it_matters: A complete light-path model explains why the same object can look different under different light sources and filters.

vocabulary.definition: wavelengths or colors present before light reaches an object
a filter letting some wavelengths pass more strongly
an object reflecting some wavelengths more strongly

lessons.written_instruction: Use four stages: identify the source, determine what the filter transmits, determine what the object reflects or absorbs, then state what light reaches the eye.

worked_examples.title: Green-filtered white card
worked_examples.problem: White light passes through a green filter and reaches a white card.
worked_examples.explanation: Green light is available after the filter and white card reflects the available green light.

guided_practice.prompt: White light passes through a red filter and shines on white paper. What color can the paper appear? Explain all four stages.
guided_practice.hint: Start by naming the light available after the red filter.

guided_practice.prompt: White light passes through a green filter and shines on a red card. Why might the card look dark?
guided_practice.hint: Ask whether red light is available after the filter.

independent_practice.prompt: A blue light source shines directly on white paper with no filter. Why can the paper look blue?
A blue light source shines on a blue object. Predict the object's appearance and explain.
A red light source shines on a green object. Predict the object's appearance and explain using available light.

exit_ticket.prompt: What is the difference between a filter changing available light and an object selectively reflecting light?
exit_ticket.answer: A filter changes which wavelengths are available by selectively transmitting them; an object then reflects some of the available wavelengths more strongly.

exit_ticket.prompt: Draw one source -> filter -> object -> eye model and label the color of light at each stage.
exit_ticket.answer: Any scientifically consistent labeled model is acceptable.

lessons.voice_prompt: Keep responses short. Ask Atticus to name source, filter, object, and eye before predicting. Make him say what light is available after the filter, then what the object reflects or absorbs. For assigned questions, never give the final answer. If his prediction is wrong, identify only the first incorrect stage and let him retry.
